Title: Unbound hukou and rebound innovation in urban China | Humanities and Social Sciences Communications
This study examines the causal effects and underlying mechanisms of hukou reform on urban innovation in cities of different sizes, using DID method based on a quasi-natural experiment by the 2014 hukou reform in China. Hukou reform can lead to an increase in urban migrants, which enhances the cultural diversity of cities, provides more informational resources, and positively influences urban innovation activities (Niebuhr, 2010 Migration and innovation: Does cultural diversity matter for regional R&D activity? Specifically, hukou reform has the greatest impact on urban innovation in cities with populations between 1 and 3 million, with an increase of 52.8%. Before the hukou reform policy was implemented, it is possible that cities with populations above 5 million and those below 5 million had different development trends in urban innovation. Model A in Fig. 4 presents the results of the parallel trends test using Eq. It shows that the difference in the level of urban innovation between the four categories of treatment and control groups prior to the hukou reform policy is statistically indistinguishable from zero. This indicates that the hukou reform has indeed enhanced the level of urban innovation in both large and small cities across China. To exclude other confounding factors of hukou policies introduced by central or local governments between 2015 and 2016 on urban innovation, we incorporated the hukou threshold index for 120 cities in China from 2000 to 2016 into the control variables, as calculated by Zhang et al. Table 5 presents the heterogeneous effects of hukou reform on urban innovation, analyzed through the lenses of geographic region, city level, innovation level, and provincial capital status. The basis for innovation differs between cities with higher or lower levels of innovation, leading to different impacts of hukou reform on urban innovation (Han et al. Journal of Economic Geography(6): 9–44")), we examined the role of hukou reform in promoting urban innovation from the perspective of regional cultural diversity in China. This study utilized an innovation index and DID approach across 282 cities from 2001 to 2016 to assess the causal effects and mechanisms of hukou system reform on urban innovation.
